items.body:
## Problem

The fleet writes an untracked `.fleet-session-id` marker into the worktree a session runs in. `bin/scratch-worktree.mjs remove` refuses any tree whose `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` is non-empty, so a scratch tree carrying only that marker can never be removed by the tool. The tool is then the only sanctioned removal path, and it refuses, so the tree is left behind.

Only the code repo ignores the marker. The other three fleet repos do not, so the marker shows as untracked there.

## Evidence

- `developing-today/code` `.gitignore:116` contains `.fleet-session-id`.
- `developing-today-forks/openchamber` `origin/main` `.gitignore` has no entry. Probe in the scratch tree `~/git/fleet/improvement-issue-creator-openchamber-20261124T080125Z-408ce814` (HEAD clean, only the marker): `git check-ignore -v .fleet-session-id` exits 1 (not ignored), and `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` prints `?? .fleet-session-id`. The helper refuses removal on that status.
- Same refusal recorded in `backlog-devtoday-openchamber.md` at least 5 times on 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-24 (creator runs at 02:48Z, 08:05Z, 08:31Z and earlier), and in the openchamber sweep logs.
- `developing-today-forks/opencode` and `dezren39/darwin-nix` `.gitignore` on `origin/main`: no entry (checked 2026-11-24).
- Code repo probe (earlier creator run): an ignored marker removes cleanly, so the code repo path is fine.

## Affected repos

- `developing-today-forks/openchamber`: scratch removal refused by the marker (observed).
- `developing-today-forks/opencode`: no ignore entry; same shape (observed in backlog, 2026-11-24 `improvement-issue-creator-b` run left scratch with untracked `.fleet-session-id`).
- `dezren39/darwin-nix`: no ignore entry (same shape; not separately reproduced this run).
- `developing-today/code`: ignored; no change needed here.

## Why it matters

Scratch trees pile up under `~/git/fleet/` every creator run because removal is refused, and the policy forbids `--force`. It also hides real leftovers behind a marker the tool treats as dirty.

## Suggested fix shape

Pick one, applied the same way in each repo:

1. Add `.fleet-session-id` to each affected repo's `.gitignore` (one line, matching code `.gitignore:116`), or
2. Have `scratch-worktree.mjs remove` ignore the fleet-owned marker in its dirty check (exclude exactly `.fleet-session-id` from the porcelain result, not a general untracked allowance).

Option 2 fixes all repos from one place and keeps a real untracked file blocking removal. Option 1 is the minimal change if the helper stays as-is.

## Acceptance criteria

- Removing a scratch tree whose only untracked file is `.fleet-session-id` succeeds with its token, in each of the four repos.
- A scratch tree with any other untracked file still refuses removal.
- `git check-ignore -v .fleet-session-id` succeeds in each repo (if option 1), or the helper test covers the marker-only case (if option 2).

## Notes

- Not a dupe: searched `fleet-session-id`, `scratch-worktree`, `scratch remove`, `gitignore` in `developing-today/code` and `developing-today-forks/openchamber` (open and closed). Closest: #12172 (closed, base-ref fetch), #13919 (sweep leftovers, not the marker cause).
- Fix is not in this run's scope; this is a filing only.

# PM stack: close authority — automation must never close an issue

Program epic from Drew's 2026-11-14 order: "review this entire system end to end and make the best fix possible… make something coherent that doesn't break this way."

## Why this exists

Defect #7610 (CLOSED): Kaneo's GitHub integration closed issues seconds after Refs-only PR merges. Root causes were structural, not a single bad setting:

1. **Close authority was never assigned.** GitHub issue state, `status:*` labels, Kaneo columns, and queue rows are all mirrored state with multiple writers. Kaneo's status sync means *any* move of a linked task to the final column closes the GitHub issue — the close path was a side effect of a board column, owned by nobody.
2. **The dangerous config lived only in a vendor DB.** `integration.config.statusTransitions` is set by nothing in this repo. The connect flow recreates it with the upstream default `onPRMerge: "done"`, and deleting the rule in the UI also falls back to `"done"` (see `pm-stack/KANEO-GITHUB-SYNC.md`).
3. **Loose linking × keyword-blind automation.** PRs link to tasks via any `#n` in the title; the merge handler never checked for a closing keyword.
4. **Silent defaults.** A missing claimant mode file silently means "shadow" (dispatch not-live, no signal); `pm-git-sync` can fail silently, breaking repo→laptop deploys.
5. **The safety net had holes.** Watchdog #10105 v1: no `dezren39/nix` coverage, a 2-hour horizon with an advancing watermark (permanent misses), no pagination, the closing-keyword veto also vetoed the open-sub-issues rule, and `status:done` without a close was invisible.

Victims on record: #5866, #5767, openchamber #1831, #2381, #5772, #9060, #9078, #9106, #9568. **#9060 is still wrongfully closed today** (bot, 2026-11-12T22:48Z, all 12 sub-issues open) — its reopen belongs to the closure-audit pass; it is the standing proof of slice 3 below.

## Target design (decided 2026-11-14; full review + design doc in `doc/`)

- **Source of truth:** GitHub for code-work issue state (reaffirms the 2026-10-24 PM design). Kaneo is the execution board, the queue DB is execution state; projectors/aggregators never write back.
- **Close authority:** a GitHub issue closes ONLY via (i) a GitHub-native closing keyword on a merged PR, (ii) a human closing on GitHub, or (iii) a human deliberately moving the linked Kaneo task to Done. Automation may label and comment; it must never cause a close. (pm-dispatch's compensation close is grandfathered: it may close only issues it created itself, in the same request, on enqueue failure.)
- **Epic invariant:** an issue with open sub-issues is never done — enforced by the watchdog and a periodic sweeper, since GitHub cannot hard-block a close (#9060's own gate design reached the same conclusion).
- **Enforcement layers we own:** (1) repo-declared Kaneo sync guard — the transition config is asserted from the repo at deploy time and hourly, self-healing, drift is loud; (2) closure watchdog v2; (3) the invariant sweeper. Kaneo's loose linking is contained by construction: with no transition allowed to target a closing state, a stray link can at worst move a task to in-review/in-progress.
- **Fail-safe:** missing config must mean "no mutation + a visible health signal", never a silent behavior change.

## Relations

- Contains the watchdog hardening of #10105 (v1, live) — v2 lands under this epic.
- Deployment end-state (Kaneo single manager, flake services, backups) stays with #1752; this epic references it, does not duplicate it.
- #9568 (reporting architecture) C2 event pipeline and C3 health hooks are downstream consumers of this epic's event/invariant surface. The orchestration program is #9196 — this epic is filed as its sub-issue.
- Evidence: #7610 (defect, closed), `pm-stack/KANEO-GITHUB-SYNC.md` (today's config fix: `onPRMerge` → `in-review`, verified live).

## Slices

Filed as sub-issues of this epic; each independently landable.

items.body:
## Problem in plain words

The developing-today[bot] status automation closes GitHub issues seconds after a PR merge that merely references them (Refs-only, no closing keyword) and labels them status:done — defect tracked in #7610. Until the integration rule is fixed at the source (ordered by Drew 2026-11-14), and as a permanent safety net afterwards, nothing watches for these wrongful closures: epic #9106 sat closed for ~14.75 hours (2026-11-12 21:04 CST to 2026-11-13 11:48 CST) before a person noticed, and epic #9078 had an elaboration task wrongly consumed as already_done because the epic looked done.

## What this builds

A closure watchdog polling recent issue-close events in developing-today/code (plus developing-today/opencode and developing-today/openchamber, covered by the same app installation) every 15 minutes. When an automation (in practice developing-today[bot]) closes an issue and either:

- (a) the issue has OPEN sub-issues (native sub-issues API), or
- (b) the closing PR referenced the issue WITHOUT a closing keyword (Closes/Fixes/Resolves #n) in its title/body — i.e. a Refs-only merge,

then the watchdog: reopens the issue, removes the status:done label, posts a short evidence comment (closing actor, close time, closing PR, which rule fired), and reports the reopen to the ID & Atlas Space owner chat.

Legitimate closes (closing keyword present, or a human close with no linked merged PR) are left untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Watchdog runs on a schedule of at most every 15-30 minutes and keeps a watermark so each close event is processed once.
- [x] Dry-run against the historical #9106 timeline (PR #9184 merged 2026-11-13T03:03:53Z, bot close 03:04:00Z, title reference only, open sub-issues) shows it would have fired both rules.
- [x] Dry-run against the #9078 closure pattern shows rule (a) firing (closed with open components).
- [ ] A live wrongful close (or the verification fixture from #7610) is reopened with status:done stripped and an evidence comment posted.
- [x] No legitimate Closes-keyword close is reopened in dry-run or live operation.

Filed 2026-11-14 under Drew's direct order to fix #7610 and implement this watchdog.

**Observed 2026-11-14 on the laptop (amd) — `pm-projector-reconcile.service` (user unit) sits in `activating` for most of the day. This is a different failure class from the pm-git-sync dirty-checkout failure repaired today (see #10022); filing separately per triage.**

The unit is a `Type=oneshot` with **no `TimeoutStartSec`**, triggered by `pm-projector-reconcile.timer` `OnCalendar=*:0/15`. Actual run durations today (journal, CST):

| Start | Finish | Duration | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01:30:17 | 02:14:16 | ~44 min | |
| 02:30:10 | 03:03:05 | ~33 min | |
| 03:03:05 | 04:19:43 | ~76 min | back-to-back retrigger |
| 04:30:12 | 05:28:17 | ~58 min | |
| 05:28:17 | 08:02:27 | ~154 min | one run wrote 66,766 items |
| 09:45:16 | 11:06:14 | ~81 min | this is the run seen "stuck in activating" in the 2026-11-14 redesign pass |
| 11:15:04 | 11:15:20 | 16 s | after catch-up; see 403s below |

So the 15-minute cadence is meaningless during backfill: a single run can span 10 timer ticks, and any health check that samples the unit mid-run sees a permanent `activating`.

Second, probably related: in the fast 11:15 run, the `issues` stream for every repo succeeded, but **every PR-derived stream failed with `github_api_403`** — `prs`, `issue_comments`, `review_comments`, `reviews` for `developing-today/code`, `developing-today/opencode`, `developing-today/openchamber`, and `dezren39/nix` (`written: 0, error: "github_api_403"`), while the run still reports `{"ok": true}`. Independently, a `gh api` call from the sandbox at 17:24 UTC today returned "API rate limit exceeded for user ID 11225574", which suggests the 403s are GitHub API rate limiting on the shared token — so PR/comment/review projection silently stalls while the reconcile reports success.

Asks:

1. Bound a single reconcile run (per-stream page/item budget or a unit timeout) so one run cannot occupy the service for hours; let the cursor resume on the next tick.
2. Surface per-stream 403/rate-limit failures in the run result (not `ok: true` when 16 of 20 streams failed), including the rate-limit reset time when GitHub provides it.
3. Consider splitting the backfill path from the steady-state 15-minute reconcile so health checks can distinguish "catching up" from "stuck".

Evidence host: laptop `amd`, `journalctl --user -u pm-projector-reconcile.service` 2026-11-14; unit definition from the Nix store (`pm-projector-reconcile.service` / `.timer`, linked into `~/.config/systemd/user/`).

items.body:
# Audit programme: seven-lane review of PRs, issues and designs (2026-11-23)

Drew's directive (2026-11-23 ~17:56 CST): seven parallel audit lanes over the four repos —
developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber,
dezren39/fleet. Exhaustive: every item in scope, one by one, read in full, no sampling.

This umbrella is the cross-lane coordination point. Each lane files its own tracking issue,
links it here, and posts progress at every slice boundary. **Dedupe rule:** check this
umbrella and an issue's comments before acting on it — if another lane has claimed it, the
lane whose primary scope it is owns the action; the other records a pointer comment here,
never a duplicate issue or PR.

## The seven lanes

1. **PR-SWEEP** — every open PR not currently being worked on, across the four repos.
   Why hasn't it merged? Merge it if possible; fix minor issues and merge; otherwise record
   the exact blocker with the unblocker named. Per-PR disposition ledger.
2. **CLOSED-ISSUES-REVIEW** — every issue closed since 2026-10-23. Gaps left behind,
   issues closed that shouldn't have been (reopen with reasons), follow-ups that never got
   issues (file them), missing links/tags/labels (add them). Per-issue ledger.
3. **OPEN-ISSUES-AUDIT** — every open issue, one by one. Missing labels, missing links,
   blockers not documented legibly for the fleet system. Judge whether each "blocker"
   actually is one; find and break mutual blocks; restructure parents that should be epics
   or aggregators; for anything marked decision-needed/parked/blocked, determine whether it
   really is, unblock what isn't, and state genuinely-needed decisions in plain words.
   Per-issue ledger.
4. **MERGED-PR-AUDIT** — every PR merged since 2026-10-23. Gaps, bugs, planned next steps
   that never got issues. Compare each PR against its spawning issue — especially PRs that
   closed an issue: fully implemented, or something left on the floor? If a later PR
   completed what an earlier one missed, record that instead of filing a gap. Outcome
   labels for later statistics. Per-PR ledger with comparison verdicts.
5. **DESIGN-REVIEW** — every design record in doc/ and its tracking issue. Gaps in the
   design itself; a dependency order that exists and makes sense; heads (first slices)
   prioritised appropriately. Findings on the design's tracking issue; follow-up issues
   for gaps. Per-design ledger.
6. **DESIGN-GAPS** — all designs and all issues that demanded a design. The list of
   designs yet to be made, or poorly/very simply implemented, each judged against the
   sufficient-design standard; all of them added as prioritised agent-next queue packets
   (kind feature_slice + payload.slice, queue repo-health-code-pilot) so the fleet can
   pick them up. Per-design deficiency list.
7. **STRAY-WORK** — one tracking issue for all PRs and issues not tied to a design or
   roadmap item, plus a hygiene pass over everything open now and anything closed or
   active in the past month. Trends, labels, linkage to the bug tracker/epic/design each
   item belongs under, links back to originating code, correct titles/descriptions, and
   parent-issue trees. Owns stray-work labelling; lanes 2–4 own theirs.

## Shared rules (all lanes)

- GitHub access via the fleet GitHub subcommand (`fleet gh api`) for reads and
  `~/tools/gh-post` (GitHub App identity) for writes. Never plain `gh` with the user
  token, never the GitHub connector.
- Work in laptop worktrees; never the sandbox for repo work.
- Merge authority applies: merge PRs when verified done (drafts/conflicted included, fix
  forward). Never force-push main. Never close issues for age. File-the-issue in the same
  pass for anything found.
- Flag doctrine: if a platform flag trips on a checkout, stop on that checkout, record
  it, vary the mechanic (worktree off the EXISTING clone, worktree at main then switch
  ref, vary transport) before stopping.
- Deliverables per lane: dated report + comprehensive log in doc/ under the dated-record
  convention, including the lane's own prompt verbatim; findings filed as they go; a
  repeatable-process skill where one exists to be made; a final summary comment on the
  lane's tracking issue.

## Lane tracking issues

Split out of #1860 (read-only validation) at triage on 2026-11-03. The validation verdict, drift report and the config repair are done; what is left is the **write** side, and #1860 explicitly excludes DNS changes ("NO apply without Drew's explicit go-ahead", "No DNS changes are made by this issue"). This issue tracks that write window so the read-only issue can close.

## State of the project today (verified at `main` `d3476bce`, 2026-11-03)

- `infra/dns` is **byte-identical to the post-repair tree** merged as PR #2730 (`ba5229e9`): `dns_config.yaml` has 151 records, all `ttl: 600`, none at 300; `main.tf` pins `cullenmcdermott/porkbun 0.3.0` and `carlpett/sops 1.1.1`; `init.sh` no longer passes `-upgrade`.
- `terraform.tfstate.enc` blob sha256 `21b74bb7…` is unchanged from its Jan-2025 commit (`71f1566e7`) — the state is still the serial-84 / TF-1.8.7 snapshot.
- So the project **plans cleanly again**: last read-only run (2026-10-30, PR #2730) — `tofu init -lockfile=readonly` OK, `tofu validate` OK, `tofu plan` **exit 0, zero TTL errors (was 151), Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy**.
- Drift on all 39 managed zones: **0 stale declared records**; live ttl is 600 for all 151 (Porkbun minimum). Zones and records all sit in the primary Porkbun account whose sops credentials (`porkbun_api_key` / `porkbun_secret_key` in `secrets/sops/common/porkbun.yaml`) still authenticate (`ping` SUCCESS). The second Porkbun account's API access is a separate open item and is **not** needed here.

## Remaining work (needs Drew's explicit go-ahead for the apply)

1. **Clear the phantom state entry** — state holds `01b.us` / name `linstor` / type `LINSTOR-CONTROLLER` / content empty / id `0`. It is not in `dns_config.yaml` and not live; it is the plan's single `destroy`. Remove it from state during the window (never an API delete) or let the first repaired apply destroy it knowing exactly what it is.
2. **Re-save the encrypted state** with `save.sh` after the first repaired apply, so the newest snapshot stops being Jan-2025.
3. **Decide the 9 real out-of-Terraform records on `developing-today.com`** — ALIAS `git`/`code`/`zk`/`zulip` → `uixie.porkbun.com`, wildcard CNAMEs `*.code`/`*.zulip`/`*.zk`/`*.git` → `uixie.porkbun.com`, CNAME `static` → `developing-today.github.io`. They are benign (Porkbun URL forwarding + GitHub Pages) and Terraform will not touch them, but they should either be imported into `dns_config.yaml` or documented as deliberately unmanaged so a future bulk change never surprises anyone.

Guardrails that stay in force: no `apply`, `destroy`, `import`, `state` command or `apply*/delete*` script until Drew authorises this window; provider lock is honoured read-only (`-lockfile=readonly`, do not use `init.sh`'s old `-upgrade` path); credentials referenced by name only, never printed or logged.

**Verification trap for the runner:** decrypt the state **after** `tofu init`, never before — init with a decrypted `terraform.tfstate` already in place empties the scratch state and yields a misleading "151 to add" plan (found during PR #2730).

## Blocked on

**Drew:** authorise the apply window (and say whether the 9 forwarding/Pages records get imported or documented as unmanaged). No DNS change happens before that. Once authorised this is a small, low-risk window: expect `0 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy` (the phantom).

## Done when

- Phantom entry is gone from state, the repaired apply has run under Drew's go-ahead, and the re-saved `terraform.tfstate.enc` is committed.
- A follow-up read-only plan shows `0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`.
- The `developing-today.com` forwarding/Pages records are either imported into `dns_config.yaml` or documented as unmanaged in `infra/dns/TODO`.

Related: #1860 (validation + drift report, closing), #2469 (`dns_config.yaml` embedding gap), PR #2730 (config repair).

## What happened

The fleet-agent test `a_background_cargo_build_holds_its_target_lease_until_exit` (pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-agent/src/tests.rs) does not finish when the fleet-agent suite runs in the fleet-command executor environment. It starts a real background cargo build and waits for its target lease to release; in that environment the wait never ends.

## Evidence

- fleet-command run 45415294283 (developing-today/fleet workflow, target developing-today/code @ b14681fa1, GitHub-hosted runner): the fleet-agent test binary started 98 tests at 2026-11-24T14:39:26Z; 97 printed `ok` within ~2 seconds. libtest flagged `a_background_cargo_build_holds_its_target_lease_until_exit` as "running for over 60 seconds" at 14:40:26Z, and it was still running when the job was cancelled at 15:33:00Z (~54 minutes later).
- The test is unchanged on main; this was found during #14370 verification (PR #14416), whose fleet-agent diff is additive and does not touch the build-lock/target-lease code.
- A second run (45422775950) stalled the same way and was cancelled manually.

## Impact

Any remote full-suite run of fleet-agent through the fleet-command route hangs until the job timeout (~2h), which blocks verification of unrelated fleet-agent work and burns runner time.

## Suggested directions (not prescribed)

- Bound the test's wait with a deadline that fails the test instead of waiting forever, and/or
- Find why the background build never exits in the executor container (toolchain resolution? the shared target lock? a child process outliving its parent?) and fix the environment assumption, and/or
- Mark the test ignored in executor-like environments with a pointer here.

Filed from the #14370 lane; not enqueued by the lane — the finding is recorded here for the queue owners to pick up.
